answers.answer: Separate the Conflict cards by I/II/III backs. Shuffle all four III cards and put them at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five on top; shuffle the three I cards and deal one on top. This makes a 10-card deck: one I, five II, four III. Return unused cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: In both games, two Agents start on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) starts next to the board; three troops start in the player's garrison and the player takes 1 water. The score marker starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place two Agents on your Leader and your third Agent (your Swordmaster) next to the game board”; “on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space”; “place three [troops] in ... garrisons”; “Take 1 water.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. After revealing, you skip the rest of your turns that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the Reveal boxes of cards revealed from the remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both types of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: “you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents” and “Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped”; Reveal Turn: Resolve Reveal Effects apply to “just-revealed cards only”; Clean Up moves “all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.”

answers.answer: No. The destination cost must be paid immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the played card, so the card's Agent effect cannot first provide resources for that cost. One card can send only one Agent, using only one of its Agent icons. A card without Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn and may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs “immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played)”; “You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents”; a card with no Agent icons “can't be played on an Agent turn.”

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison, for at most five troops. At a non-Combat space you cannot deploy units to the Conflict. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison; units from the garrison can be deployed only at a Combat space.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: the cube icon recruits a troop “take it from your supply and place it in your garrison”; at a Combat space deploy “any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more units from your garrison.”

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate lets you recall a Spy from a connected post to send an Agent to a space occupied by another player. Gather Intelligence lets you recall a connected Spy just after placing an Agent, before receiving space or card effects, to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence; two different Spies may do so. Gather Intelligence must be chosen immediately after placing the Agent and before effects are received.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy icon sends to a connected space and “you do not recall the Spy”; Infiltrate recalls a Spy to ignore another player's Agent; Gather Intelligence is chosen “immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)”; “You cannot recall the same Spy to both.”

answers.answer: Two troops give 4 strength, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4, for 11 total. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0 even if you have revealed swords. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in Combat Intrigue, which is limited to players with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; “You must have at least one unit in the Conflict to have any strength; if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.” Combat Intrigue is for each player with “at least one unit in the Conflict.”

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent you from playing Combat Intrigue later if an opponent acts. The window closes when all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, at which point Combat resolves. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not their garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: “You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; resolve once players “pass consecutively.” After rewards, troops return to “supply (not their garrison)” and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: In a four-player game, if exactly two players tie for first, both take the second reward; neither wins or takes the Conflict card, and the remaining players compete for the third reward. In a three-player game, both tied players take the second reward, but no other rewards are given and no one takes the Conflict card. A player with zero strength cannot receive a reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players each gain the second reward and “no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card”; with four players, if exactly two tie, “remaining players compete for the third reward”; with three or fewer, no other rewards. A “0 strength” player receives no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles the rewards taken; a second worm does not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. When a doubled reward offers the option to pay for something, the cost may be paid a second time for a second gain: for example, pay 3 spice for 1 VP, or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: “if you have one or more sandworms ... double the rewards”; control and battle icons cannot be doubled; an optional reward cost “may [be paid] a second time”; example says “3 spice to gain 1 VP, or 6 spice to gain 2.”

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card into your supply, check for a match. A matching icon on another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply qualifies. Matching is mandatory: flip the matching pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild icon can match any one of the three battle icons in your supply; flip the pair face down for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card, check for “another face-up Conflict or Objective card” with the same icon; if so, you “must” flip the pair for 1 VP. During Endgame the wild icon matches any one of the three.

answers.answer: Reaching 2 Influence gives 1 VP, which is lost if Influence drops below 2. Reaching 4 gives the track bonus, which is retained even if Influence later falls below 4; it can be earned again by dropping and advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance token and its VP. Tying the holder at 4 does not take the token: it transfers only when an opponent rises to a higher space, and the prior holder loses the VP while the new holder gains it.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: reaching 2 gives 1 VP “(lost if you drop back below 2)”; reaching 4 gives the track bonus and “you do not give the bonus back”; Alliance token passes if an opponent rises to a “higher” space.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects during the Reveal turn. It may be pooled from multiple sources to buy one card and split from one source across different cards. The Imperium Row is replenished to five cards, so the replacement can be bought immediately if affordable. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: use Persuasion “before, between, or after” Reveal effects. Acquiring Cards: may pool or split Persuasion; after replacing a missing Row card, “you may acquire its replacement”; acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.

answers.answer: At the Makers phase, put 1 spice on each Maker space with no Agent; this accumulates with prior bonus spice, and an Agent sent to a Maker space gains all bonus spice there. Maker Hooks are obtained at Sietch Tabr and are usually a requirement for summoning a sandworm. A sandworm cannot be summoned to a Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains; after its detonation removes the Shield Wall, it may be summoned to any Conflict. A sandworm is placed directly in your Conflict quadrant and can never be placed in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers: each Agent-free Maker space gets “1 spice” added to any previous bonus, and visiting gains all there. Sandworms: Maker Hooks token is obtainable at Sietch Tabr and usually required; sandworm icon puts it in your Conflict quadrant and it “can never be placed in a garrison.” Shield Wall protects the three named locations until removed.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, reaching 10 or more VP or having an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare Victory Points. Ties are broken in order by spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “At the end of a round” the 10 VP or empty-deck condition triggers Endgame; “First, players may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue”; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has two contracts face up and the remaining 18 face down. It adds four Intrigue cards and four Imperium cards. Shaddam Corrino IV is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are specifically for use with Rise of Ix, not this standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle 20, flip “two face up,” put “remaining 18 face down”; shuffle 4 additional Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards; Shaddam “is not required.” The Rise of Ix subsection says its 10 additional contracts are “used specifically with Rise of Ix.”

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. If all contracts have been taken by players, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the amount of spice shown that turn in total, including other sources; Immediate is completed as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow is completed when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts describes taking one of two face-up and replacing it; if all are taken, the icon reverts to 2 Solari. Completing contracts defines Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow as stated.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for the space where you already sent your Agent this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. When completed, announce it, gain its listed rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: announce completion, “gain the rewards it shows,” flip it face down, and “leave it in your supply.” If acquired after sending the Agent to that space, “you must wait until a future turn.”

answers.answer: Unsupported by the supplied summary. It says one- and two-player games require the separate Rivals rules supplement and that this rulebook summary does not detail those modes; it does not state the Rival count, Ornithopter Objective assignment, First Player assignment, turn order, or whether a Rival Reveals.
answers.evidence: Overview: “Games for one or two players require the separate Rivals rules supplement; ... this rulebook does not detail those modes.”
